name: LP-MSPM0G3507 LaunchPad development kit
sources: MSPM0G350x datasheet SLASEX6C (features list); LaunchPad user guide SLAU873E (board parts, header silkscreen; R59/R60 not fitted on schematic page 20)

columns.head: The chip: MSPM0G3507
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M0+
Runs the program, up to 80 million steps a second (80 MHz)
Flash: 128 kB
Holds the program. Kept when the power is off
RAM: 32 kB
Working memory while it runs. Cleared at power off
Power: 3.3 V on this board
The chip accepts 1.62 to 3.6 V, so 5 V parts need care

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: GPIO: up to 60 pins
Plain on/off pins: LEDs, buttons, control lines. 35 reach the board's headers
SPI: 2
Fast bus with a clock and data wires: displays, SD cards, memory chips
I2C: 2
Two-wire shared bus: sensors and touch chips, each with its own address
UART: 4
Simple serial text, one wire each way: GPS, the computer's terminal
ADC: 2 / DAC: 1
Measure a voltage / make a voltage, 0 to 4095 steps (12-bit)
Timers: 7, CAN-FD: 1
Timing and PWM for dimming and motors / the car and factory network bus

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
USB debug probe, red LED, color LED, 2 buttons plus reset, light sensor, temperature sensor
Headers
40 pins in four rows (J1 to J4), the standard BoosterPack layout
Not on the chip
No Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. No USB port of its own: the USB plug talks to the debug probe
Not fitted
Pull-up resistors for I2C (R59, R60). With the chip's internal pull-ups, software I2C works and the I2C block did not; external resistors were not tried
